subtitle.text: "Moo! Moo!"
Mr. Mann heard his cows mooing in the field.
He ran outside and saw something flash across the sky.
It shot straight toward his farm.
"Oh no!" cried Mr. Mann.
"Yuck!" said Jack.
"We're having sloppy joes for lunch today."
It was Monday morning at Metro City Elementary School.
The students were on their way to class.
"Sloppy joes are the worst," said Mara.
"They're so gross and they drip everywhere."
"I wish Rocket Girl was here," said Terrell.
"She could save us from those sloppy joes."
"Yeah, Rocket Girl can do anything," said Jack.
"Rocket Girl is the number one superhero in Metro City," said Mara.
"She can fly, she's really strong, and she can shoot lasers out of her eyes.
She has lots of other super powers too!"
"Last week she stopped a big monster from stomping the school," said Terrell.
"Rocket Girl once saved Metro City from giant robots," said Mara.
"Remember when moon men were planning to blow up Earth?" asked Jack.
"Rocket Girl flew to the moon and destroyed their Earth Blaster!"
"You guys are always talking about Rocket Girl," Roxy said quietly.
"But she's not perfect.
She can't save us from sloppy joe day."
"Are you kidding?" asked Mara.
"I'll bet you're just jealous, Roxy," said Terrell.
"Jealous?" asked Roxy.
"Yes," said Terrell.
"You're jealous because you're never around when Rocket Girl shows up.
You probably wish you were Rocket Girl."
"Me? Rocket Girl?" Roxy laughed.
"That's a ridiculous idea!"
Just then Roxy's watch beeped.
It was only loud enough for Roxy to hear, and no one else.
"I'm tired of talking about Rocket Girl," Roxy told her friends.
"I'm going to see if Principal Penn needs help with anything."
Roxy walked down an empty hallway and made sure no one was around.
Then she pressed a button on her watch.
A small screen blinked on.
Mayor Bloom, the mayor of Metro City, appeared.
He didn't look happy.
"What's wrong, Mayor?" asked Roxy.
"A strange object landed at Mr. Mann's farm," said Mayor Bloom.
"We think it might be a spaceship."
"A spaceship? With aliens?" asked Roxy.
"We're not sure," said Mayor Bloom.
"But whatever it is, we need to find out.
I talked to Principal Penn.
She said you can leave school until we solve this case.
We're counting on you, Rocket Girl."
"I'm on my way," said Roxy.
Roxy ran into an empty room.
A moment later she was Rocket Girl!
Sometimes Roxy felt bad that her friends didn't know she was actually Rocket Girl.
But Roxy had decided to tell her secret only to Mayor Bloom and Principal Penn.
That way she could still have a normal life.
Well, sort of normal.
How many eight-year-olds had to save the world every day?
But now was not the time to worry about that.
Rocket Girl had a job to do!
Roxy ran down the hall and out the front door of the school.
"Okay," she said.
"It's time to figure out what landed at Mr. Mann's farm."
Then Roxy blasted into the air.
"Look out the window!" cried Mara.
"Rocket Girl!" said Terrell.
Soon Roxy was at Mr. Mann's farm.
She looked around.
Some of the corn had been cut down.
Roxy didn't see the spaceship though.
Just then something moved in the cornfield.
A figure stepped toward her.
"Oh no!" Roxy laughed. "It's an alien detective!"
"This is no time for making jokes," said Detective Smith with a frown.
Detective Smith was Metro City's head detective.
He was a very serious man.
He never joked.
"Fine," said Roxy. "So what happened here?
Where's the spaceship?"
"I don't know," said Detective Smith.
"I looked all over for it.
I didn't see it anywhere."
"Did Mr. Mann see where it went?" asked Roxy.
"No," said Detective Smith.
"He got scared and ran into his house.
He told me he hid under his bed.
When he came back out, the spaceship was gone.
So was the corn."
"Why would the aliens take the corn?" Roxy wondered.
She looked around.
She saw a tree with a broken branch and flew over to it.
"It looks like something crashed into this tree," thought Roxy.
Nearby, a fence was also broken.
Roxy looked from the tree to the fence.
Then she looked past the fence.
She could see a trail of damaged trees.
"I bet the spaceship did that," thought Roxy.
"But why didn't the spaceship fly over all the trees?
And where did the spaceship go?"
Roxy flew up high to get a better view.
The trail led straight toward . . .
Roxy gulped.
"Uh-oh! I know exactly where the spaceship went.
It's headed toward downtown Metro City!"
"Rocket Girl!" called Detective Smith.
"Where are you going?"
"I'm going back to town!" yelled Roxy.
"That's where the spaceship went!"
Roxy flew as fast as she could.
When she reached downtown Metro City, she saw people running.
"Agh! Aliens are attacking!" shouted a tall man.
"Run for your life!" someone cried.
"Save us, Rocket Girl!" yelled an old woman with blue hair.
Roxy saw lots of scared people.
But she didn't see the spaceship anywhere.
"Where did the spaceship go?" Roxy wondered.
A large group of people ran by.
They were all wearing Shop Well Supermarket uniforms.
"Aha!" thought Roxy.
"The spaceship must be at the Shop Well Supermarket."
Roxy flew to the Shop Well Supermarket.
And then she saw it—the spaceship.
It had crashed into the front of the store.
Why did the spaceship keep crashing into things?
Two green aliens came out of the store.
Roxy hid behind a parked truck.
The aliens had cans of tomato soup.
Roxy watched one alien open a small door on the side of the spaceship.
The alien poured the soup into a hole.
The other alien got into the spaceship and tried to start the engine.
The spaceship lifted off the ground for a second.
But then smoke puffed out of it.
Boom! The spaceship crashed into a parked truck.
"Hmm," thought Roxy.
"Maybe the spaceship runs on food."
Another alien came out of the store with jars of applesauce.
It dumped the applesauce into the hole in the spaceship.
Again the aliens tried to start up the ship.
This time it flew for a moment, and then crashed into a mailbox.
"The food doesn't seem to be working though," Roxy thought.
"I wonder why."
The aliens started talking to each other.
One was waving its arms around.
Another was beginning to yell.
"Uh-oh," thought Roxy. "The aliens don't look happy."
One of the aliens spotted a pizza delivery truck driving by.
The alien pointed a small device at the truck.
Shlurp!
A stream of purple slime shot out.
The truck's wheels instantly stuck to the road!
"Help, Rocket Girl!" the driver shouted as aliens surrounded the truck.
Roxy raced toward the aliens.
But before she could reach them, Roxy saw one alien point the device at her.
Shlurp!
Roxy looked down.
The purple slime made her feet stick to the street!
"Grr!" Roxy used her super strength.
She pulled, heaved, and twisted until—shloop!—her feet came unstuck.
By now the aliens had opened the door of the pizza delivery truck.
"Yikes!" the driver shouted.
"Stop right there!" Roxy shouted as she flew toward the aliens.
"I'm not going to let you hurt him."
"We aren't going to hurt anyone," said one alien.
"My name is Brim.
We need to refuel our spaceship.
It runs on food, but none of this food is working."
"Why not?" asked Roxy.
"It's not the right kind of food," said Brim.
"We need something really thick and gloppy."
"Thick and gloppy?" said Roxy. "Hmm . . ."
"Ugh!" said Mara.
"I got sloppy joe on my sleeve!"
"This is awful," said Jack.
Just then Brim and the other aliens walked into the cafeteria.
"Aliens!" someone shouted.
"Run for your life!" shouted someone else.
Rocket Girl flew in.
"Don't panic," she said. "These guys are friendly.
They just need your sloppy joes so they can refuel their spaceship."
Rocket Girl explained everything, and no one was scared anymore.
"Oh! You can have my sloppy joe!" said Jack.
"Mine too!" said Mara.
"Take mine!" said Terrell.
"Everybody, grab your lunch and follow us," said Rocket Girl.
"Try it now, Brim," said Roxy.
Brim started up the spaceship.
It worked perfectly.
"Thank you, everyone," said Brim.
"Those sloppy joes are the perfect fuel for our spaceship."
The kids waved good-bye as the spaceship flew away.
"I'm glad we got rid of those sloppy joes," said Terrell.
"But now what will we eat?"
"Look out the window!" said Mara.
"Pizza!" said Jack.
Mayor Bloom came into the cafeteria.
He had a tall stack of pizzas.
"Thanks for giving up your lunches to save Metro City," he said.
"I have pizza for everybody."
The students cheered.
A moment later Roxy entered the cafeteria.
"Roxy!" said Mara. "You missed Rocket Girl!"
"And aliens!" said Jack.
"What?" asked Roxy, pretending to be surprised.
"Where were you?" asked Mara.
"Oh, I was helping Principal Penn with . . . office work," said Roxy.
Terrell looked at Roxy suspiciously.
"Well, you know what, Roxy?
You were wrong.
Rocket Girl was able to save us from sloppy joe day."
Roxy didn't say anything.
She just smiled and quietly reached for a slice of pizza.
It was early morning at Dairy Dream Ice Cream Parlor.
Miss Dipper, the owner, arrived at the store.
She unlocked the door and turned on the lights.
She gasped.
"My ice cream is gone!"
"I think I'm melting!" said Mara, wiping her forehead.
"Don't talk," said Jack.
"It only makes you feel hotter."
The air conditioning at Metro City Elementary School wasn't working.
The students in Miss Apricot's class were miserable.
It was Quiet Reading Time, but no one could concentrate on reading.
"It's so hot, I can't even think," said Terrell.
"Me neither," said Jack.
"I wish we could go swimming."
Jack closed his eyes and imagined jumping into an ice-cold pool.
"I wish we could have ice cream," said Mara.
"That would cool us off."
"If only Rocket Girl was here," said Terrell.
"She could do something about this heat."
"This heat isn't so bad," said Roxy.
"Are you kidding?" asked Terrell.
"Aren't you hot right now?"
"Of course," said Roxy.
"But I have a secret power I use to keep cool."
Terrell looked interested.
So did everyone else.
"You do?" said Jack. "Tell us!"
Terrell, Jack, and Mara leaned closer to hear about Roxy's secret power.
Roxy looked very serious. "I'll tell you.
But you all have to promise to never tell anyone," she said.
"We promise," said her friends, hardly breathing.
"Okay," Roxy whispered.
"It's very simple.
When it's really hot, I . . ." She paused.
"You what?" asked Mara. "What do you do?"
Roxy looked around to make sure no one else was listening.
She whispered, "I try not to think about it."
Roxy giggled.
Jack groaned.
"I thought you were going to tell us something good!"
Miss Apricot looked up from the front of the room.
"I know it's very hot," she said.
"But please be quiet."
"I still think Rocket Girl could stop this heat," whispered Terrell.
Just then Roxy heard her watch beeping.
"It's the mayor," she thought.
"Miss Apricot," said Roxy. "May I go to the restroom?"
A moment later Roxy was in the girls' room.
"Mayor Bloom," she said, looking at the screen on her watch.
"What's the problem?"
"Rocket Girl, we need your help!" said Mayor Bloom.
"True Savings Bank is being robbed.
I spoke with Principal Penn.
She said you're excused from class until we solve the case."
"I'm on my way," said Roxy.
Roxy quickly changed into Rocket Girl.
She ran out of the school and shot up into the air.
"Look!" said Mara. "It's Rocket Girl!"
"I wonder where she's going," said Jack.
"Roxy's still not back from the restroom," said Terrell.
"What's taking her so long?"
When Roxy arrived at True Savings Bank, she expected to find the bank robber.
Instead she saw a crowd of people.
And they were all frozen!
"Whoa! What happened here?" Roxy wondered.
"Why are all these people frozen?"
Detective Smith rushed into the bank.
He was out of breath from running.
"Rocket Girl," he said.
"I came as fast as I could.
I was at the Dairy Dream Ice Cream Parlor."
"You know, Detective, you really shouldn't eat ice cream for breakfast!"
Roxy laughed.
Detective Smith frowned.
"I wasn't eating ice cream for breakfast," he said.
"The ice cream was stolen.
So we have two robberies to solve."
"Hmm," thought Roxy.
Dairy Dream had been robbed.
And there were frozen people at the bank.
Roxy found this very suspicious.
"I think both robberies were done by the same person," said Roxy.
"Why do you think that?" asked Detective Smith.
"We have stolen ice cream and frozen people," said Roxy.
"The crimes must be connected."
"I don't think so," said Detective Smith.
"Bank robbers don't usually rob ice cream parlors."
"Well, we have to unfreeze these people right away," said Roxy.
"I'll use my heat vision."
"Heat vision?" said Detective Smith.
"I thought your eyes shot lasers."
"They do that too," said Roxy.
"You'd better stand back, Detective."
Roxy stared hard at one of the frozen people.
An orange beam slowly radiated out of Roxy's eyes, melting the ice.
She melted one ice block after another.
Soon all the people were free.
"Brr! Thank you, Rocket Girl," said a woman.
"Can you tell us what happened here?" asked Roxy.
The woman shivered.
"I came in to deposit a check," she said.
"Then a man came in and started blasting freeze rays at everyone. Brr!"
"Freeze rays?" said Roxy.
Just then Detective Smith's phone rang.
"Hello?" he said.
Detective Smith looked very serious.
"Really? How long ago?
Oh no! This is terrible.
Yes, sir. Right away, sir."
"What's wrong now?"
asked Roxy after Detective Smith had hung up.
"Another bank is being robbed!" said the detective.
"What bank is being robbed now?" asked Roxy.
"Metro City Central Bank," said Detective Smith.
"We have to hurry—Rocket Girl?"
A minute later Roxy was outside Metro City Central Bank.
It was a large building in downtown Metro City.
It was at the top of a long, steep hill.
Inside the bank Roxy could see people running around and crying out.
"He's shooting freeze rays!"
"I'm so cold!"
"Save us, Rocket Girl!"
Roxy saw the villain.
He was wearing silver boots and a white jumpsuit.
Icicles hung from his silver beard.
"It's Freddie Freeze!" said Roxy.
Freddie was holding a Big Freeze Blaster.
It was attached to a large tank on Freddie's back.
He was walking toward the bank's safe.
Roxy used her x-ray vision to look in the tank.
It was filled with ice cream.
"Aha!" Roxy realized.
"Freddie Freeze is using the ice cream to power his Big Freeze Blaster!"
Roxy flew into the bank.
"Hold it right there, Freddie!" she shouted.
"Your bank-robbing days are over!"
Freddie Freeze quickly turned around.
His eyes widened in surprise.
"Rocket Girl!" he said. "You'll never stop me!"
Freddie blasted a freeze ray at Roxy.
Fwoosh!
Roxy jumped out of the way and ran back outside.
Freddie followed her.
Roxy ran partway down the hill.
"I'm going to turn you into an ice pop!" shouted Freddie.
Fwoosh!
The tree next to Roxy was frozen solid.
"You'll never hit me!" said Roxy.
"You're too slow!"
Freddie Freeze shot blast after blast of freeze rays.
Roxy darted back and forth and up and down.
She was much too quick for Freddie.
"Just give up, Freddie," said Roxy.
"I'm too fast for your dumb freeze rays."
Roxy was now standing at the edge of the hill.
Freddie aimed his Big Freeze Blaster and fired at her.
Fwoosh!
Roxy jumped.
"Ha-ha!" Roxy laughed. "You missed me again! Whoa!"
Freddie's last freeze ray had frozen the entire street.
It was a long, steep hill, and Roxy was sliding fast!
"Whoa!" cried Roxy.
Roxy tried to melt the ice with her heat vision.
But she was sliding too fast and spinning all over the place.
Looking up, she could see Freddie aiming his Big Freeze Blaster at her.
Roxy gulped. "Uh-oh!"
Freddie Freeze pulled the trigger of the Big Freeze Blaster.
Nothing happened.
"Drat!" said Freddie.
"I used up all the freeze power dealing with that pesky Rocket Girl.
But never mind her—I need to get more ice cream.
I have a lot of banks to rob today."
Roxy finally stopped sliding when she reached the bottom of the hill.
"Whew!" she said, standing up.
Roxy flew back to the top of the hill.
Freddie was gone.
"Freddie must have gone to get more ice cream," thought Roxy.
"He already robbed Dairy Dream.
What other place in Metro City has a lot of ice cream?"
Roxy thought for a moment and then gulped.
"Oh no! The Metro City Elementary School cafeteria!"
"Ugh! It's hotter in the cafeteria than in our classroom," said Mara.
All the students had just sat down to eat.
Today's lunch was hot meatball sandwiches.
"Eww. Hot food is the last thing I want right now," said Jack.
Suddenly the doors to the cafeteria flew open.
"Rocket Girl!" shouted a boy.
"Listen up, everyone!" said Roxy, landing next to the ice cream freezer.
"We don't have much time.
I need you to start eating lots and lots of ice cream!"
The whole cafeteria became silent for a second.
Then a boy spoke up.
"We need to eat lots of ice cream?" he asked.
"Yes!" said Roxy. "And quickly!"
She started throwing ice cream to the students.
"Why?" asked another student.
"Who cares why?" said Terrell. "Let's just eat!"
Ice cream cones, ice cream sandwiches, and ice cream pops flew through the air.
Soon everyone was eating ice cream, even the teachers.
"Woo-hoo!" shouted Terrell.
"This is great! I'm finally cooling off."
"I love ice cream!" said Jack.
When Freddie Freeze burst into the cafeteria, all the ice cream was gone.
"Aargh!" cried Freddie.
Roxy smiled.
"Freddie, you're not going to need that Big Freeze Blaster anymore.
You're going to jail!"
After Roxy took Freddie Freeze to the police station, she headed back to school.
The kids were outside for recess.
"Roxy! Where have you been?" asked Mara.
"I was helping Principal Penn work on the school website," said Roxy.
She got on a swing and started swinging.
Terrell gave Roxy a suspicious look.
"Rocket Girl came while you were gone," he said.
Roxy just smiled as she flew high in the air.
It was early one evening.
Principal Penn and the teachers were arriving at Metro City Grand Hotel.
A mysterious man named Mr. Sweeps had invited them to a special meeting.
"Maybe he's going to donate money to the school," thought Principal Penn.
"Welcome," said Mr. Sweeps.
"Please take a button."
Principal Penn pinned a star button onto her jacket.
Then she sat down.
"Now," said Mr. Sweeps.
"Let me tell you why I invited you here . . ."
It was a beautiful fall morning.
Roxy and her friends were walking to school.
"I hope the weather stays like this," said Jack.
"Our class has a field trip to the zoo next week."
"I can't wait to see the snakes," said Terrell.
"I'm worried we won't be able to go to the zoo," said Mara.
"My mom told me our school needs money.
The field trip to the zoo might be canceled."
"That would be awful!" said Jack.
"We should do something to help."
"What can we do?" asked Mara.
"We don't have any money."
"Maybe Rocket Girl can help," said Terrell.
"I don't think so," said Roxy.
"Rocket Girl doesn't have money."
"Rocket Girl can do anything," said Terrell.
"She's the greatest superhero ever!"
Roxy shrugged.
Soon Roxy and her friends reached school.
Roxy looked at the parking lot.
"Where are all the teachers' cars?" she wondered.
"Welcome, students!" said a man at the school entrance.
He was handing out star-shaped buttons.
"I'm Mr. Sweeps, your substitute principal today.
Principal Penn is . . . um . . . busy doing other things."
Roxy looked at Mr. Sweeps suspiciously.
Something about the substitute principal seemed odd.
"Cool! Thanks for the button!" said Jack.
Mr. Sweeps handed one to Roxy.
"Here you go, young lady," he said.
"Thanks," said Roxy, carefully looking at the button.
"Go ahead, put it on," said Mr. Sweeps.
Just then Roxy heard her watch beep.
She put the button in her pocket.
Then she hurried away from the school's entrance.
Roxy pressed a button on her watch.
"Mayor Bloom," she said. "What's wrong?"
"We have a problem, Rocket Girl," said the mayor.
"Principal Penn disappeared.
I want you to find out what happened to her."
Roxy looked over at Mr. Sweeps.
"Don't worry," said Roxy. "I'll find Principal Penn."
Roxy made sure no one was watching her.
Then she sneaked around the school building.
In an instant she was Rocket Girl!
"It's time to find out what happened to Principal Penn," said Roxy.
She blasted off into the sky.
"Look! It's Rocket Girl!" said Mara.
"I wonder where she's going," said Jack.
Terrell looked around.
"Does anyone know where Roxy went?" he asked.
Roxy landed at Police Headquarters.
She found Detective Smith.
He was sitting at his desk, watching something on his computer.
"Are you watching a TV show?" Roxy laughed.
"Aren't you supposed to be solving crimes?"
Detective Smith frowned.
"I'm not watching a TV show.
I'm watching video from a traffic camera."
"I got a call from Mayor Bloom," said Roxy.
"He said Principal Penn disappeared."
"She didn't disappear," said Detective Smith.
"She left town.
In fact, all the teachers from Metro City Elementary School left town. Watch this."
Roxy watched the video from the traffic camera.
The video showed lots of cars and buses driving by.
"Hey! That was Principal Penn!" said Roxy.
"Keep watching," said Detective Smith.
Next Miss Apricot drove by.
Then Mr. Green drove by.
One after another, all the teachers from Roxy's school drove by.
"That's West Street," said Detective Smith.
"It leads out of Metro City and into the mountains."
"So all the teachers drove to the mountains?" asked Roxy.
"I think so," said Detective Smith.
"But it doesn't make any sense.
Why would teachers do that on a school day?
They're supposed to be teaching!"
Roxy watched the video again.
This time she noticed something.
All the teachers were wearing the same star buttons!
And the buttons were glowing.
"I've seen those buttons before!" cried Roxy.
"Mr. Sweeps, the substitute principal, was giving them to all the students!"
"Are you sure about that?" asked Detective Smith.
"That is very suspicious.
We'll have to . . . Rocket Girl?"
In a flash Roxy was back at Metro City Elementary School.
She burst through the front doors.
"Where's Mr. Sweeps?" Roxy demanded.
The hallway was empty.
"Hello?" Roxy called.
No one answered.
Roxy ran into her classroom.
No one was there.
No one was in the principal's office either.
Roxy soon realized the whole school was empty.
"Where did everyone go?" she wondered.
"I'll use my super hearing."
A second later she heard something—something very strange!
Drip . . . drip . . . drip . . .
Chirp! Chirp! With her super hearing, Roxy heard lots of usual school sounds.
She heard water dripping from the art room sink.
She heard a cricket chirping in one of the kindergarten rooms.
But she also heard something unexpected.
It was a deep voice coming from under the school.
"Work! Work! Work!" growled the voice. "Move faster!"
"That's Mr. Sweeps!" gasped Roxy.
"I knew I shouldn't trust him!"
Roxy ran down the stairs to the basement.
She came to a pair of locked doors.
Roxy stared hard at the doors.
Lasers shot out from her eyes.
Whiz-hoo!
The doors blew apart, and Roxy ran through the opening.
The basement was empty.
Roxy glanced around and spotted a trapdoor.
She rushed over and opened it.
Roxy jumped down, landing in a large cavern.
There, Roxy saw all the students hard at work.
Some were chipping away at the rock walls with pickaxes.
Others were pushing wheelbarrows.
"Is this a mine?" Roxy wondered.
She looked around some more.
She saw one student pull something sparkly from the wall.
"Whoa!" gasped Roxy. "This is a diamond mine!"
The students were all wearing the star buttons from Mr. Sweeps.
Nobody looked at Rocket Girl.
They were all too busy working.
"This is totally weird," Roxy said to herself.
She saw Terrell.
"What's going on here?" Roxy called to him.
Terrell didn't answer.
He didn't even look at her.
"He's hypnotized!" Roxy realized.
"Everybody is. It's because of those star buttons."
Suddenly Jack and Mara sneaked up from behind and grabbed Roxy.
She thought about fighting them off.
But Roxy knew that wasn't a good idea.
She didn't want to hurt her friends.
Mr. Sweeps appeared.
"Thought you could stop me, did you?" he said.
Roxy noticed he was wearing a glowing, star-shaped ring.
"What's going on down here?" Roxy demanded.
"There are lots of diamonds here under your school," said Mr. Sweeps.
"And I want them!
I hypnotized your teachers and made them leave town.
Then I hypnotized your schoolmates so they could mine the diamonds."
Mr. Sweeps let out a cackle.
"I am going to be rich!"
"You'll never get away with this!" said Roxy.
Mr. Sweeps grinned. "Oh yes. I will!"
He looked at Jack and Mara.
"Bring the prisoner this way!"
Jack and Mara pushed Roxy into a cell.
Mr. Sweeps smiled. "Now you'll never stop me."
He slammed the heavy iron door.
Roxy heard him lock it.
Roxy thought about the ring Mr. Sweeps was wearing.
"He's using that ring to control everyone.
I need to destroy it."
Roxy looked around the cell.
"I could break down that door," she thought.
"But Mr. Sweeps will hear me.
I need a way to sneak up on him."
Roxy kicked at the rock floor to see how hard it was.
"I think I have an idea."
Mr. Sweeps was examining a diamond when he heard a crash.
"Rocket Girl is trying to break out of her cell," he yelled.
"Everyone, guard the door!"
All the students dropped their tools.
They gathered in front of the cell door.
Boom! There was a deep rumbling sound.
The entire cavern shook.
"As soon as Rocket Girl comes out, capture her!" commanded Mr. Sweeps.
Suddenly—kaboom! Pieces of rock flew everywhere.
Roxy blasted through the cavern floor behind everyone.
Mr. Sweeps spun around, but he wasn't fast enough.
Whiz-hoo! Roxy fired her eye laser beams.
The ring exploded.
"My ring!" cried Mr. Sweeps.
Instantly the students' buttons stopped glowing.
"Where are we?" asked Jack.
"What's going on, Rocket Girl?" asked Mara.
"You were all hypnotized by Mr. Sweeps," answered Roxy.
"He isn't really a principal.
He was forcing you to mine diamonds here under the school."
"That's right," said Detective Smith, who had just walked into the cavern.
"And now Sweeps is going to jail!"
In a flash Rocket Girl disappeared.
A moment later Roxy appeared.
She was wearing her regular clothes and her star button.
"What happened?" she mumbled, pretending she'd been hypnotized too.
Terrell gave her a suspicious look.
The next morning Principal Penn and the teachers were back at work.
"It looks like things are back to normal," said Mara.
"I'm glad," said Jack.
"I'd rather learn than work in that diamond mine."
"You know what else?" asked Mara.
"We can go to the zoo!
My mom told me our school has money for field trips now."
"Where did the money come from?" Terrell asked.
"Principal Penn is going to sell the diamonds!" said Mara.
"Wow!" said Terrell.
"I told you Rocket Girl can do anything.
She helped our school get money!"
Roxy didn't say a word.
Everyone at the TV station was busy.
A woman turned on a camera.
A man carried a microphone.
They were getting ready to film an episode of Mighty Man.
"Where's Mighty Man?" asked someone.
"Here I am," said an actor in a superhero costume.
Suddenly—poof! A man appeared in a puff of smoke.
He had a tall hat and a thin moustache.
He wore a tuxedo.

Roxy arrived at the office.
It was in an old factory.
A big man sat behind a desk.
He wore overalls and a hard hat.
"Jack Hammer!" Roxy shouted.
The man stood up. "Hello, Rocket Girl."
Roxy frowned. "Why are you trapping people in their houses?"
Jack snorted. "Why do you think? I want to steal stuff.
And it's not just houses.
Recently, I worked on police headquarters and a school."
Roxy narrowed her eyes. "What school?"
"Metro City Elementary." Jack Hammer looked at his watch.
"In fact, I should probably head over there now."
"Grr!" Roxy rushed toward the villain.
He stepped quickly through a door.
Roxy burst through and found herself in a large, empty room.
"Huh?" The room spun, and Roxy was thrown against a wall. "Oof!"
When the room stopped spinning, Roxy ran through another door.
Mirrors surrounded her.
Her reflection was everywhere.
Roxy gulped. "I'm stuck in an evil fun house!"
She heard Jack Hammer laugh.
"You'll never get out, Rocket Girl!"
Roxy took a step. Bam!
She hit a mirror.
All of her reflections rubbed their heads.
"Ugh! I'm stuck in an enormous mirror maze!"
"Yes, you are!" Jack Hammer appeared in the mirrors.
Whiz-hoo! Roxy fired her eye laser beams.
Ping! Ping! The beams bounced off the mirrors.
Roxy ducked as they passed by her head.
Jack Hammer laughed. "So long, Rocket Girl!"
Roxy banged into mirrors again and again.
After a few minutes, she was still in the maze.
"How will I get out of here?" Roxy thought.
Then she had an idea.
She blew her freeze breath.
The mirrors filled with frost.
Cracks crept along the glass, and then—Smash!
The mirrors shattered.
Roxy saw an exit sign. "Yes!"
Metro City Elementary School was empty when Roxy arrived.
She called Terrell's phone.
Using her super hearing, she heard it ringing.
Roxy rushed to the phone and sighed.
It was in their classroom, inside Terrell's backpack.
Terrell, however, wasn't there.
Walking through the school, Roxy used her super hearing again.
She heard voices directly under the gym.
Roxy punched through the floor.
Beneath the floor there was an enormous funnel.
Roxy jumped in and went down a long, twisting slide.
Everyone was at the bottom, trapped in a big empty room.
"Rocket Girl!" Terrell said.
"Whew!" Principal Penn wiped her brow. "You found us!"
Roxy brought everyone back to safety.
"Now I have to find Jack Hammer!"
Roxy spotted the builder behind the school.
He was loading school computers into a van.
"Stop right there!" Roxy shouted.
"Never!" Jack Hammer fired a nail gun at Roxy.
"Yikes!" Roxy fired her eye laser beams.
Jack Hammer ducked.
The beams bounced off his hard hat and shattered a window.
"Ha-ha!" The villain hopped into his van and took off.
Roxy shot after him.
Flying alongside the van, she used her heat vision.
The van's doors melted shut.
"Hey!" Jack Hammer yelled.
Roxy zapped the tires with her eye laser beams.
The van slid through a puddle and stopped.
Jack Hammer tried to open the door. "Oh no! I'm—"
"Trapped!" Roxy smiled.
Roxy took Jack Hammer to jail.
Next she flew to his building.
All the stolen items were there.
Finally she returned to school.
"How was indoor recess?" Roxy asked her friends.
"It was great!" Mara said.
"Yeah!" Jack said. "There's a big slide under the gym!"
Roxy and Terrell shot each other a quick look and smiled.
"This is such a lovely day."
A woman was with her neighbors.
They were having a party on the roof of their apartment building.
A man smiled. "I'm glad we got rid of that smelly hawk's nest."
Another neighbor grinned. "Our building is much nicer now."
Kee, kee! A winged figure swooped down from the sky.
"Ahh!" The woman screamed.
"Cool!" Jack said. "Vultures!"
Roxy and her friends were at the Metro City Raptor Center.
The center had lots of raptors in large cages.
A woman walked over.
She wore a name tag that read Robin.
"Those are turkey vultures," Robin said.
"Vultures are a type of raptor.
Raptors are birds that hunt other animals."
"Why are they here?" Mara asked.
"Those vultures got injured," Robin said.
"We helped them get better.
Soon we'll release them back into the wild."
Robin led everyone to another large cage.
"This is Perry. He's a peregrine falcon.
Perry's wing is broken. We think he got hit by a car."
"That's awful," Jack said.
"The person driving the car didn't even stop."
Robin's eyes flashed with anger.
"People need to be nicer to birds, especially raptors.
Raptors are great hunters with amazing eyesight.
Vultures even help the environment by cleaning up dead animals."
"There's a bird's nest outside my window," Terrell said.
"I love looking at the baby birds."
"Well, some people don't like nests!"
Robin looked very angry now.
"There was a beautiful hawk's nest on an apartment building near Metro City Park.
The building's horrible residents had the nest removed!"
"That stinks," Jack said.
Suddenly Robin looked up.
A large bird was flying overhead.
"I'll be right back." Robin hurried away.
"That was strange," Mara said.
Jack shrugged.
"It's sad that the hawk's nest was removed," Roxy said. "I love hawks."
"Me too," Jack said.
"Why didn't anyone stop those people from removing it?"
"Rocket Girl could have stopped them," Terrell said.
Mara rolled her eyes.
"I'm sure Rocket Girl has more important things to do, Terrell."
Roxy and Terrell looked at each other and grinned.
Roxy's watch beeped.
She stepped away from her friends.
"Mayor Bloom? Is something wrong?"
"Rocket Girl, I need your help."
The mayor looked annoyed.
"Workers are trying to cut down some trees in Metro City Park.
They were just attacked. All their equipment was destroyed."
"Don't worry, Mayor," Roxy said.
"I'm on my way!"
"I have to get to Metro City Park," Roxy thought.
"Someone just attacked workers there."
Roxy looked at her friends.
"I'll be right back. I'm going to go, um, look at the owls again!"
When Roxy landed in Metro City Park, she saw some workers.
Broken saws and rope lay in the grass.
A bucket truck was parked nearby.
Its tires were flat, and its windows were smashed.
Its crane was bent.
"Wow," Roxy thought.
"Why would someone do this?"
Detective Smith was looking at some trees.
Vultures were perched on the branches.
"So, Detective," Roxy said with a grin.
"Do the vultures know who attacked the workers?"
Detective Smith groaned. "Very funny, Rocket Girl.
Those are the trees the workers were going to cut down."
A worker walked over to Detective Smith and Roxy.
"I'm Earl," he said. "I'm the supervisor."
"What happened here?" Detective Smith asked.
Earl scratched his head.
"Well, we came here to cut down those trees.
But then a flying person attacked us."
"Why were you cutting down the trees?" Roxy asked.
"Vultures perch in them," Earl said.
"Residents near here don't want vultures around."
Roxy was confused.
"What's wrong with vultures? They're just birds."
Earl shrugged. "The residents say the vultures are creepy."
"Um, can someone help me?" a voice said suddenly.
Roxy looked up.
A worker was high up in a tree.
A rope lay in the grass below him.
"Carl!" Earl said. "I forgot you were up there!"
Carl looked annoyed.
"That bird villain snapped my rope. Now I'm stuck up here!"
"Hold on!" Roxy flew up to Carl and brought him safely down.
"You're the best, Rocket Girl," Carl said.
Detective Smith took out his notepad.
"Can either of you describe the villain?"
Earl nodded. "Yeah. She looked like a hawk.
She had really big wings and a hawk mask."
Carl nodded too. "She called herself Thunderhawk."
Detective Smith looked thoughtful.
"This must be the same person who attacked people at the roof party.
The party was over there."
He pointed at a nearby building.
"The residents said they had just gotten rid of a hawk's nest."
"Hmm," Roxy thought.
"Robin cares about birds, especially raptors.
Maybe she knows who Thunderhawk is."
She called Terrell.
"Hey, Rocket Girl," Terrell said.
"I'm coming back to the Raptor Center, Terrell," Roxy said.
"I need to talk to Robin."
"Robin's not here," Terrell said.
"She never came back."
"Wow," Roxy thought.
"I wonder if Robin is Thunderhawk."
She looked over at Detective Smith.
"Detective," Roxy said, "I think—"
The detective's phone rang.
"Hello? Oh no! We'll be right there!"
Detective Smith looked at Roxy.
"Thunderhawk is at Metro City Zoo.
What were you going to tell me?"
"Never mind," Roxy said.
Zoom! Roxy flew off.
When Roxy arrived at the zoo, people were running in every direction.
"There's a big hawk person!"
"Run for your lives!"
Roxy spotted Thunderhawk.
The villain was perched on top of the bird building.
She had large wings and a hawk mask.
"That's definitely Robin," Roxy thought.
"Thunderhawk!" she shouted.
Robin looked over.
"Go away, Rocket Girl! I'm freeing these birds!"
The villain smashed a hole in the building's roof.
Birds flew out.
"You can't do that!" Roxy shouted.
"Birds shouldn't be in cages!" Robin cried.
"They should be free!"
"You won't be free for much longer, Thunderhawk," Roxy said.
"You're going to jail!"
Roxy shot toward Robin.
She reached out to grab the villain.
Robin leaped. Roxy missed her.
"Hurricane wind!" Robin shouted.
She flapped her huge wings.
Whoo-whoo-whoosh!
A strong wind blew.
Roxy tried to stay where she was.
But the wind was too strong.
Roxy tumbled backward, crashing through the fence of a gorilla exhibit.
"Oof!" Roxy sat up and looked around.
A gorilla looked at her.
Then it jumped out of the exhibit and ran off.
"Uh-oh!" Roxy said.
She already heard people shouting and screaming.
"A gorilla's loose!"
"Run for your lives!"
Roxy crawled out of the exhibit.
Robin swooped over the crowd of screaming people.
"I have to stop Robin," Roxy thought.
"But that gorilla is on the loose!"
Roxy flew after the gorilla.
She saw a zookeeper approaching the animal.
The zookeeper glanced up at Roxy.
"Don't worry, Rocket Girl!
I'll take Melvin back to the gorilla exhibit.
Just stop that villain, please!"
Roxy flew over the zoo.
"Where did Robin go?" she thought.
Then she saw a stampede.
Elephants, rhinos, and other animals were chasing people all over the place!
Roxy heard laughter.
Robin was flying away.
"Good luck catching all those animals, Rocket Girl!"
Roxy helped gather the zoo animals.
"Now I have to find Robin," she thought.
Roxy flew to the Raptor Center.
She spotted Terrell, Mara, and Jack.
But Robin wasn't in sight.
Roxy landed on top of the main building.
Peeking through a window, Roxy saw Robin.
The woman still wore her hawk disguise.
Roxy leaped through the window.
"I've got you, Thunderhawk!"
Robin gasped. Then her face had a nasty look.
She raised her wings. "Hurricane—"
Zoom! Roxy charged at the villain.
They crashed through the wall and landed on the ground below.
"Rocket Girl!" Mara cried.
As Roxy and Robin wrestled, Terrell watched anxiously.
Finally Roxy pinned Robin to the ground.
"Give up, Thunderhawk!"
Robin let out a cry. "Kee, kee!"
Roxy was confused. "What are you doing?"
Robin ignored her. "Kee, kee!"
With a rushing sound, raptors swooped down.
They clawed at Roxy.
"Hey!" Roxy waved her arms to protect herself.
"What's going on?"
Robin slipped free. "I can speak to birds, Rocket Girl.
I protect them, so they protect me!"
Roxy tried to shoo away the raptors.
"I don't want to hurt these birds," she thought.
"Rocket Girl!" Terrell cried. "Use your super breath!"
Roxy saw that Terrell was standing near a large open cage.
Whoosh! She blew.
Her super breath swept the birds into the cage.
Terrell threw the door shut.
Robin flew off.
Whiz-hoo! Roxy's eye laser beams burned Robin's wings.
"Ahh!" Robin fell from the sky.
Roxy flew fast and caught her.
"Rocket Girl!" Robin said. "You . . . saved me!"
Roxy brought Robin down to the ground.
"I care about birds too," Roxy said.
"But you're still in trouble."
Robin hung her head. "I just wanted to help birds."
"I have an idea," Roxy said.
First, Rocket Girl and Thunderhawk visited Mayor Bloom.
Robin told him how vultures help the environment.
"Very well," the mayor said.
"We won't cut down the trees in the park."
Next, they visited the apartment building.
Robin told the residents how amazing hawks are.
The people looked upset.
"We're very sorry about the nest," a woman said.
After that, Robin promised Roxy she wouldn't cause any more trouble.
"And I'll pay for all the damage."
The next day Roxy and her friends were in Metro City Park.
"Cool!" Jack said when he saw vultures in the trees.
Roxy smiled.
Then she looked up at the apartment building.
A hawk was starting to build a new nest.
